hr_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me draft an offer letter for my company's first employee hire. Before drafting, ask me for any missing details: candidate's full name, job title, employment type (full-time/part-time/exempt/non-exempt), start date, base salary or hourly rate, reporting manager, work location (remote/office address), company legal name and address, at-will employment state (for correct at-will language), any equity/bonus terms, benefits eligibility date, contingencies (e.g., background check, reference check), and the offer expiration date for candidate response.

Using these details, draft a complete, professional offer letter that includes: company letterhead placeholder, greeting, position title and employment type, start date, compensation (salary/hourly rate and pay frequency), reporting structure, work location, summary of benefits eligibility (to be finalized separately during benefits enrollment), any equity/bonus terms provided, at-will employment statement appropriate to the specified state, any contingencies, an offer expiration date, and signature lines for both the company representative and the candidate.

Flag clearly any sections where you made assumptions or used placeholder language (e.g., standard at-will clause, generic benefits summary) so I can review and adjust before sending.

When the draft is complete, save it as a document (Word or Google Doc format) and report back with: the full draft text or a link to the saved document, a bullet list of all assumptions/placeholders needing my confirmation, and any missing information you still need from me.

Do not send, email, or deliver this offer letter to the candidate, and do not mark it as final. This draft requires my explicit review and approval before it is used. Please stop for human sign-off once the draft and summary are ready.

hr_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the offer letter envelope for our first employee hire using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops/e-signature platform. Do not send anything yet — sending requires my explicit approval.

First, ask me for anything missing: candidate full name and email, job title, start date, compensation (salary, bonus, equity/option grant details if any), reporting manager, and which company signatory should co-sign. Also confirm whether we need a confidentiality/IP assignment agreement bundled with the offer.

Then, using {{vendor}} and my configured credentials:
1. Create a new offer letter envelope in {{vendor}}, selecting our standard offer letter template (and confidentiality/IP agreement and option grant template if applicable).
2. Populate all merge fields with the candidate and offer details I provided.
3. Set the signature routing order: candidate signs first, then our company signatory.
4. Attach any ancillary documents (IP agreement, option grant) to the same envelope if applicable.
5. Generate a preview of the completed envelope so I can review the exact language and field values before anything is sent.

Do not click send, submit, or finalize the envelope in {{vendor}} at any point.

When done, report back with: a summary of the envelope contents (documents included, recipients, routing order), a link or reference to the draft envelope in {{vendor}} for my review, and a short checklist confirming all fields are correctly populated. Then stop for human sign-off — I will personally review and trigger the send once I approve the draft.

hr_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me track the 'candidate accepts offer' step in our hiring process. The candidate has received an offer letter and we are now waiting on their decision, which typically takes 1-3 days. This is a person-dependent, asynchronous step — the actual acceptance decision remains a human step and cannot be driven by you.

Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing details you need: candidate name, email address, the date/time the offer was sent, the offer expiration date (if any), and which channel was used to send it (email, e-signature tool, etc.).
2. Prepare a simple tracking record (a checklist or short status doc) noting: candidate name, offer sent date, expected response window (1-3 days), and offer expiration date.
3. Draft a polite, professional follow-up email I can send to the candidate if no response is received by the expected window, checking in on their decision. Do not send it — just prepare the draft for my review.
4. If I give you access to check email or a shared inbox, monitor for a reply from the candidate indicating acceptance, decline, or a request for more time, and summarize what you find when I ask you to check.
5. Do not attempt to contact the candidate directly, sign anything, or make commitments on my behalf.

When you're done preparing the tracking record and the follow-up draft, report back with: (a) the tracking record contents, (b) the drafted follow-up email text, and (c) a note confirming that actual candidate acceptance is a third-party decision outside your control and remains a human step to monitor. If I ask you to check for updates later, poll the inbox or ask me for the candidate's response status and report what you find.

hr_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me add my first employee to {{vendor}} (my payroll platform) as part of our hiring process, using my already-configured {{vendor}} credentials. Approval is required before any change is finalized, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off before submitting or activating the record.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the new employee's full legal name, personal email, start date, job title, department, employment type (full-time/part-time/exempt/non-exempt), pay rate or salary, pay schedule, work location/state, and manager. Also confirm whether I want the employee invited to complete a self-serve onboarding flow (collecting their W-4, I-9, and bank details directly) or whether I'll enter that information myself.

Then, using {{vendor}}'s employee onboarding tools (dashboard or API), draft the new employee record with compensation and tax setup details pre-filled based on what I provided, and prepare (but do not send) the self-serve onboarding invite if requested. Check for any missing required fields (e.g., SSN, address, tax elections) and flag them clearly rather than guessing.

Do not create, submit, or activate the employee record, and do not send any invitations, until I explicitly approve. Present me with a summary of the fully prepared record — all fields, compensation, tax setup, and onboarding flow status — formatted as a clear checklist so I can review accuracy before approving.

When finished, report back with: (1) a summary of the drafted employee profile and settings, (2) any missing or ambiguous fields you flagged, (3) confirmation that no data was submitted or activated yet, and (4) a note that this remains a human step pending my sign-off to finalize in {{vendor}}.

hr_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me set up the payroll schedule for our first employee hire in {{vendor}}, our payroll platform. Approval requirement: a human must explicitly approve before any changes are applied to the live payroll system, so you must prepare everything but not finalize or submit it.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our {{vendor}} account access (use your configured credentials), the employee's team/department, desired pay frequency (weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, or monthly), the intended first pay date, and whether this schedule should apply only to this employee's team or across multiple teams.

Then do the following:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using your configured credentials.
2. Navigate to the payroll schedule configuration area (dashboard or API, whichever is available).
3. Draft the proposed pay schedule configuration(s) — including frequency, pay period start/end logic, and pay dates — for the relevant team(s), supporting multiple concurrent schedules if we have more than one team with different cadences.
4. Prepare a clear summary showing: schedule name, frequency, first pay date, affected team(s)/employee(s), and any default settings {{vendor}} applies (e.g., weekend/holiday shift rules).
5. Save the configuration as a draft or pending change within {{vendor}} if that option exists, rather than activating it.

Do not submit, activate, or confirm the payroll schedule — this step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, so stop for human sign-off once the draft is prepared.

Report back with: the proposed schedule details, any {{vendor}} default settings applied, a link or reference to where the draft/pending configuration lives in {{vendor}}, and a short checklist of what I need to review and approve before it goes live.

hr_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me manage the 'Employee completes I-9 and W-4' step of hiring my first employee, using {{vendor}} as our payroll/onboarding platform. Completing the actual I-9 and W-4 forms — including the employee logging in, entering personal data, and signing — remains a human step that only the new hire can perform; do not attempt to fill in, sign, or submit any part of this on their behalf.

Please do the following instead:
1. Ask me for any missing details: the new hire's name and personal email, their start date, and confirmation that our {{vendor}} account is set up for self-service onboarding.
2. Using our configured credentials, check whether a self-serve onboarding flow has been sent to this employee in {{vendor}} that collects W-4, I-9, and bank details. If not yet sent, prepare the invite (draft the onboarding packet/checklist with the employee's info pre-filled where the platform allows) and note that sending it requires my confirmation — then stop for human sign-off before sending.
3. Once sent, monitor {{vendor}} periodically (poll or check status) to see whether the employee has completed and submitted their I-9 and W-4.
4. Do not enter, edit, or attest to any of the employee's personal, identity, or tax information yourself.

Report back to me with: current status (not sent / sent & pending / completed), the date last checked, and any errors or missing information blocking progress. If the forms are completed, confirm so I can proceed to the next hiring step (payroll and benefits setup).

hr_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me set up benefits enrollment in {{vendor}} (our payroll platform) as part of hiring our first employee. Before starting, ask me for any of these you don't already have: our {{vendor}} account login context (I will use my configured credentials), the new employee's census details (name, date of birth, address, hire date, employment type), our company's desired benefit offerings (e.g., health insurance tiers, whether we want to offer a 401(k)/retirement plan), and any budget constraints or employer contribution preferences I have in mind.

Then, using {{vendor}}'s benefits administration area:
1. Enter or confirm the employee census data needed for benefits enrollment.
2. Pull up available health insurance plan options in {{vendor}} that match our stated preferences, and summarize the plans, coverage tiers, and estimated employer/employee costs.
3. Pull up available 401(k)/retirement plan options in {{vendor}}, noting contribution matching structures and how they sync to payroll.
4. Pre-fill the enrollment forms for the employee with their census data and the shortlisted plan options, but do not select a final plan or submit any commitment.
5. Prepare a clear checklist showing: employee data entered, plan options identified, estimated costs, and what remains to be confirmed.

Because selecting specific benefit plans creates a recurring financial commitment for the company, you must not choose a final plan, enroll the company, approve costs, or submit anything on my behalf. Once the census data is entered and plan options are prepared, present the checklist and options summary to me and then stop for human sign-off.

When you report back, include: what census data was entered, the list of plan options found with cost estimates, confirmation that no plan has been finalized or submitted, and the specific next action you need from me (e.g., which plan to select) before enrollment can proceed.

hr_001:n8.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the creation of a new company email account in Google Workspace for my first employee. This step requires my explicit sign-off before anything is applied, since granting a new credentialed account is a security-sensitive action.

First, ask me for any missing details you need:
- New employee's full legal name
- Desired email address / username (or a proposed format like first.last@mydomain.com if I haven't decided)
- Their job title and department
- Which organizational unit or group they should belong to in Google Workspace (if we use OUs/groups)
- Any specific license type they should be assigned
- Recovery/secondary contact info if required
- Start date, so the account can be scheduled or noted accordingly

Once you have these, go to https://admin.google.com/ using my configured credentials and open the new-user creation form. Fill in all fields (name, desired email/username, organizational unit, license assignment, department/title metadata) exactly as I specified, but do NOT click the final create/save/confirm control. Take a screenshot or capture the filled-out form state so I can visually verify every field before it goes live.

Prepare a short summary listing: the exact email address to be created, the OU/group assignment, license type, and any other settings you entered, so I can review them at a glance.

Then stop for human sign-off — do not submit, approve, or finalize the account creation yourself. I will review the prepared form and summary, and I will personally click create/save in the admin console.

Report back with: the summary of prepared values, confirmation that the form is filled but not submitted, and the screenshot/capture for my review.

hr_001:n9.prompt:
You are helping me add our newly hired employee to our {{vendor}} team-chat workspace as part of onboarding. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) the new employee's full name and work email address, (2) confirmation of which {{vendor}} workspace to use if I have more than one, and (3) which channels they should be added to (e.g., general, team-specific, or private channels) and at what membership level (member vs. admin/guest).

Using our configured credentials, please: 1) Prepare a workspace invitation for the new employee via {{vendor}}'s admin dashboard or documented API, using their name and email. 2) Identify or confirm the public and/or private channels they should join based on their role, and prepare the membership/channel assignments accordingly. 3) Draft a short welcome message for posting in the relevant channel(s) once they join. 4) Compile a summary showing: the employee's name/email, the workspace they'll be invited to, the channels and access levels proposed, and the draft welcome message.

Do not send the invitation or add the employee to any channels yet — this step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied. Prepare everything listed above, present it clearly, and then stop for human sign-off. Report back with the full summary of what you prepared (invitation details, channel/membership plan, and welcome message) so I can review and approve before you proceed.

hr_001:n10.prompt:
You are helping me grant stock options to our new hire using {{vendor}}, our equity-management platform. Before starting, ask me for: the new hire's full name and email, the number of options to grant, the vesting schedule (e.g., standard 4-year with 1-year cliff, or any custom milestones/acceleration terms), and our {{vendor}} issuer ID if not already configured in your credentials.

Using your configured credentials for {{vendor}}, please:
1. Confirm the new hire exists as a stakeholder in {{vendor}} — if we use an HRIS/payroll system (e.g., Gusto, Rippling) that syncs to {{vendor}}, check whether the hire has already synced over; if not, ask me how I'd like to add them.
2. Create a draft option grant for this hire via {{vendor}}'s programmatic interface, specifying the option count, the vesting schedule I gave you, and using the current 409A-compliant strike price on file.
3. Leave the grant in draft/pending status — do NOT attempt to approve, finalize, or submit it for board approval yourself. This step requires board sign-off and the gate must stay in place.
4. Pull a summary of the draft grant (via {{vendor}}'s list/view of option grants) to confirm the details are correct — recipient, quantity, strike price, vesting terms, and status.

When done, report back to me: the draft grant ID/reference, the hire's name, option count, strike price, vesting schedule, and current status (should read something like 'pending board approval' or 'draft'). Include a short checklist of what still needs human action (e.g., 'board must review and approve this grant'). Do not approve, sign, or submit anything on my behalf — stop for human sign-off once the draft is prepared and verified.
